chapter: The craft of the ad lib player
title: What shapes an ad lib player's performance
summary: Hall says an instrument is an extension of oneself, influenced by people, mood and family discipline.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, relevant to this whole situation, you said there were some things you wanted to talk about in general about what a musician has to do after he learns to play his instrument.

Right. In this form of music, which is an ad lib form of music -- I won't say that it's jazz because that would be confining it to one line. I think a little more flexible than that. But the difference between being a symphony player and being a person to play ad lib was that the symphony player was disciplined bar by bar to make this B flat, and it was an impersonal B flat. I'm just using B flat as a note, because my star pupil, Mike Slattery, I used to give him hell about B flat, so he calls himself B flat Mike.

But the notes themselves has a lot to do with the people that surround an ad lib player more than the discipline of a symphony player. And this is how you create a lifestyle, as to how you play. Your instrument is only an extension of yourself, and yourself is in the society that you're surrounded with.

So these people have an influence on how you -- how you play, how you sound, not directly but emotionally. You can leave the house mad or leave the house glad and have a different performance on the bandstand.
Uh-huh. And you can come into the club and be influenced by the atmosphere and the people.
Of the people that are there.
And people who you're working with.
And the people who come to hear you?

Right. You have a whole scope of things that are going through -- unconsciously going through your mind. You can -- all of these factors have a bearing on what you're playing, and you can still be worrying about paying the rent.
You know, whether you're going to get paid that day or not. Any of those things.
But family life has a lot to do with it. I came from a very disciplined family, so my playing is disciplined. I feel miserable if I make a mistake, sound bad, you know, to myself.
